data.narrative:
Asimov is a Series B biotech company that has raised $209M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage biotech firms, with particular focus on 3 same-sector peers at Series C stage: Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $209M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression, implying $397M. Peer-median analysis anchors to the three Series C comparables, yielding a median valuation of $3.8B (range: $3.1B–$10.3B). Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, common among private companies.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $338M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The wide spread reflects material divergence between stage-progression mechanics and peer-median positioning. Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage-adjustment multiplier for Asimov's specific development trajectory and the relevance of Series C peers to current Series B valuation. Revenue trajectory and clinical/commercial inflection milestones would narrow this range materially.
